scope: Independent static review of the live adapter, retained thirteen-file MVM source patch and preparation script, with targeted provisioning/campaign review. No builds, tests or VM launches were run by this reviewer.

findings.finding: Inbound open enforces the global envelope bound but does not reject a canonical signed message whose encoded length exceeds a smaller configured capability max_queue_contribution_bytes. The outbound path enforces this grant limit; canonical MVM open checks payload scope, not queue contribution.
findings.requested_change: Reject inbound wire length above min(global envelope cap, signed configured queue contribution) before installing receiver authority; add one focused smaller-grant regression.
findings.measured_campaign_impact: The registered provisioning uses 262144 for all queue contributions, equal to the enforced global envelope cap; current pilot rows are unaffected.

findings.finding: The design states that an owner's policy lock spans endpoint handling and control-plane revocation waits for that transaction. The campaign does serialize work through one exclusive service owner, but it does not implement a policy lock spanning open/handle/reply or a concurrent control-plane update path.
findings.requested_change: Describe the actual single-owner/no-concurrent-policy-update witness and retain the documented public API concurrency limitation; do not claim a lock or update barrier that is absent.
findings.measured_campaign_impact: No campaign policy updates occur concurrently; this is an unsupported mechanism claim rather than a transfer correctness failure.

positive_checks: Canonical verified-open returns its private authenticated header only after identity, signature, capability, time and replay verification; the legacy payload API delegates without changing checks.
SentCall reply acceptance binds policy owner/generation, sender and authority keys, key id, binding id, boot, correlation, causation, transfer, sequence and compatible reply kind.
Live leases enforce both real UTC expiry with a five-second conservative margin and monotonic deadlines; generation changes invalidate previously minted proofs.
Framing caps bodies before allocation and records actual partial I/O bytes. Failed/partial operations close the owned socket. Only completely read/written frames increment frame counts.

Outbound queue caps and monotonic fixed-window message-rate counters are bounded; one call permit remains owned until the pending proof is consumed/dropped. The demonstrated receiver processes one request at a time.

The MVM mailbox service has a dedicated optional endpoint and existing bounded relay budget; missing/cleared bindings refuse, production supervisor leaves it absent, and canonical handoff does not inherit it.

Patch preparation archives only the exact committed base into a fresh output, uses quoted paths, enforces a storage reserve, validates/applies only the retained patch and does not modify the input checkout.

Campaign byte counters distinguish application data, canonical envelope bytes and stream framing. CPU/wall scopes exclude identified fixture copies and independent verification; README keeps VM lifecycle and WAN claims separate.
checked_existing_receipts: qualification/mvm-mailbox-green.exit = 0, including two focused MVM vsock mailbox tests
mvm-patch/preparation-check.json records exact-base positive preparation and existing-output/wrong-revision negative cases

independent_identity_checks.patched_source_command: shasum -a 256 -c patched-files.sha256 in the managed mvm-worktree

This review covers a development-assurance, single-owner local integration witness, not FIPS validation, CUI accreditation, general concurrent service ownership or production mailbox lifecycle.
Current retained verification receipts predate the requested narrow fixes; final verdict requires checking their source delta and root-owned regression receipts.
